_comment: English body for drake (robotics). Official README fetched 200 on 2026-11-07; unknowns kept explicit.

axes.model_access: Drake is not a model product and the official docs list no model-provider catalogue; policies or models enter through user code, LCM/ROS 2 integrations or external training frameworks. Its official positioning is a C++/Python toolbox for robot dynamics analysis and control design, with the model layer supplied by the user (2026-11-21).
axes.runtime: Drake runs as a C++/Python library inside a local process. Official support covers Ubuntu 24.04/26.04, macOS Tahoe/Golden Gate and Amazon Linux 2023, with pip, APT, binary packages and source builds; it is not a hosted cloud service and has no browser runtime (Installation page, 2026-11-21).
axes.local_files: Drake reads and writes local scenes, models, configuration and data assets; installs default to /opt/drake or a Python virtual environment. Users remain responsible for file permissions and asset licences; Drake does not manage training-data copyright, robot-workspace safety or cloud sync (official installation docs, 2026-11-21).
axes.background: Drake provides no hosted scheduler, job queue or resident server process: simulation, solving and visualisation run inside the Python/C++ process the user starts, and background execution depends on the OS and the user’s process manager. Official docs describe library build and invocation only, with no resume, distributed scheduling or job-recovery service (2026-11-21).
axes.tools: Drake centres on C++/Python APIs, with pydrake, MathematicalProgram solvers, Meshcat visualisation, LCM and ROS 2 integration. Official docs list four integration surfaces — Python, LCM, ROS 2 (unsupported) and Julia (unsupported) — and no MCP server or agent tool protocol (2026-11-21).
axes.context: Not applicable: Drake is not a chat model and has no LLM context window. State is carried by scene files, configuration, node state or checkpoints in user code; cross-session memory, prompt context and multi-turn dialogue management are outside its capability surface (2026-11-21).
axes.permissions: Permissions follow the OS and host process: Drake introduces no account, role or cloud ACL, and model/scene reads plus robot-device and network access inherit process permissions. On real hardware, emergency stop, device access and network isolation are user-configured; official installation docs list platforms and dependencies but define no unified permission model (2026-11-21).
axes.fit: Fit: robot dynamics modelling, contact/friction simulation, trajectory optimisation, control design and verification, and planning research that needs exposed equation structure (sparsity, analytical gradients, polynomial structure). Not fit: an out-of-the-box ROS navigation stack, a hosted simulation service or game-engine-style content production (2026-11-21).

runs: This entry checks the official docs for supported platforms, installation methods and integrations. Install size, solver performance and real-hardware deployment must be assessed in the project environment.
